chunks: Al-Muzaffar ibn Ja'far al-Alawi (may Allah be pleased with him) narrated to us, saying: Ja'far ibn Muhammad ibn Mas'ud narrated to us, from his father, from Hamdawayh, who said: Muhammad ibn Isa narrated to us, from Yunus ibn Abd al-Rahman, from Ibn Maskan, from Abu Baseer, who said: Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) said:
The one who knows the differences/disputes of people is not a weakened individual.
ai.seo_question: What does it mean to be 'not weakened' in Shia hadith?
ai.summary: In *Mani al-Akhbar*, Shaykh al-Saduq records Imam al-Sadiq’s (peace be upon him) insight that deep familiarity with human diversity and differing dispositions prevents one from being easily overpowered or deceived. This concept, often linked to the virtue of *al-hilma* (forbearance) and *al-waqi'ah* (situational awareness), underscores that true strength in Shia ethics lies not merely in physical power but in the intellectual and social acuity to navigate complex interpersonal dynamics. Such knowledge empowers the believer to maintain dignity and agency amidst varying societal pressures.

en.basel-kadem: 3.	We were told by Mudaffar bin Ja’far al-Alawi, may Allah be pleased with him, that he said: We were told by Ja’far bin Muhammed bin Mas’ud, from his father, from Hamdawayh, that he said: We were told by Muhammed bin Isa, from Yunus bin Abdul-Rahman, from Ibn Maskan, from Abu Baseer, that he said: Abu Abdillah, peace be upon him, said:
The one who knows the dispute, he is not a weakened individual.
